Subject: Pilot proposal: Qdrant + S3 cold-tier fallback for embeddings index

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. As discussed, BlueRidge AI (we're the systems integrator supporting the Qdrant relationship) put together a short pilot scope to validate a hybrid storage pattern: hot index in Qdrant with transparent cold-tier fallback to S3 for large, infrequently-accessed vectors.

Attached: pilot_scope_v1.pdf and an initial architecture sketch (qdrant-arch-draft.drawio).

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm Redwood runtime constraints (max sequence length, typical embedding sizes) so we can size prefix caching.
- List of acceptable auth patterns for accessing S3 from Qdrant nodes (we see both role-based and signed-temporary creds options).
- A quick compatibility sanity-check: will Redwood's batcher/kv cache play nicely with an index that can page vectors back from S3?

Proposed timeline (4–6 weeks): discovery + perf baseline (1 wk), integration adapter work (2–3 wks), joint validation and perf run (1 wk).

Can we kick off a short technical sync next week with your infra/serving engineer and anyone owning the storage product? I propose Thu 2027-04-29 16:00 UTC.

Thanks,
Sandra
Sandra Li
Senior Partnerships Manager | BlueRidge AI
Sent on behalf of BlueRidge AI and Qdrant integration team

--

Appreciate the write-up and the diagram. This aligns with a lot of customer asks we've seen around cost-tiering for embeddings. I'm looping in our infra lead (Karthik) and product-ops (Jonas) to scope the safe list of constraints.

Quick answers up front:
- We typically operate with 1536 and 4096-dim embeddings; batched tokenization is handled upstream.
- Our runtime supports both long-prefix KV caching and per-request streaming; main constraints will be peak token concurrency and cold fetch tail latency.

Karthik/Jonas — can you triage the attached pilot doc and confirm whether the proposed auth flow (temporary STS credentials handed to the adapter) is acceptable? Also please flag any risks with our KV cache interacting with an on-demand cold fetch path.

I can make Thu 04/29 16:00 UTC work for a 45m tech sync — please confirm.

Evelyn

Evelyn / team —

Read through pilot_scope_v1.pdf and the drawio. A few technical clarifications and asks from infra before the sync:

1) Cold fetch path latency SLO: what is BlueRidge/Qdrant's expected P95 for a fetch from S3 into the vector service? If >200ms we need to consider async fallback behaviors in the runtime.

2) Consistency model: will Qdrant return partial results while fetching cold vectors, or does the service block until all vectors are present? We need to know for our streaming tokenizer/batcher expectations.

3) Security: temporary STS creds are fine but we require proof points for key rotation and an audit log trace per fetch. Can BlueRidge/Acme storage confirm ability to emit signed fetch events to our audit pipeline?

4) Sample traffic: can you share a small sample trace (no customer PII) — just a distribution of query sizes and hit rates — so we can simulate batching benefits vs. raw per-call cost?

Jonas: I'd like you to own the integration test definition (SUP-2345) — will add acceptance criteria (latency, cost delta, recovery behavior).

I'll be on the Thu 04/29 16:00 UTC call.

-karthik

Subject: Re: Pilot proposal: Qdrant + S3 cold-tier fallback for embeddings index

Hi Karthik / Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick review. A few direct answers and notes from the Qdrant engineering perspective:

- P95 cold fetch: in our internal tests we see ~120–180ms (us-east region) for a single-object GET from S3 with optimized transfer (range requests + warmed TLS). That assumes object sizes in 2–8KB range typical for 1536-d embeddings quantized to int8.

- Consistency: Qdrant can return partial result sets (it streams available hits) while issuing background fetches for cold shards. We expose an explicit flag the client can use to request blocking behavior if desired.

- Audit/logs: Qdrant-side fetch events can be emitted and proxied into a cloud audit sink. We will work with Acme Cloud Storage to ensure S3 access logs are enabled.

- Sample traces: attaching a short compatibility note and a tiny synthetic trace that mirrors our pilot sample. See attached qdrant-sdk-compatibility-notes.md.

Two practical asks before the kickoff:
1) Provide a test S3 bucket + read role (or a short-lived token exchange flow) so we can run a baseline perf run.
2) Confirm acceptance criteria for the joint perf experiment (we suggest: maintain <5% tail-latency regression at 99th percentile vs hot-only baseline and <12% delta in per-query cost).

Looking forward to Thu.

—Alexei
Qdrant Integrations
